answer: Clones share one owner and one domain. Each key publishes the epoch nonce, the word pearl or sable, in a TXT record on a domain it controls, and the ledger resolves it twice, ten minutes apart, rejecting TTLs under 300 seconds since a cached answer proves no control. One zone, one key; keys resolving through the same nameservers get clustered. Fifty identities mean fifty registrations near $10 a year, about $500 before one attestation, and fifty zones live inside the window. A miner with one honest name holds the ticket. Harbor fees run this way: one berth is cheap, fifty are not.
